summary: H.R. 4368 authorizes the Caribbean Basin Security Initiative (CBSI) to be carried out by the Secretary of State and the Administrator of the U.S. Agency for International Development. The bill aims to promote citizen safety, counter transnational criminal organizations, strengthen law enforcement and the rule of law, prevent crime among at-risk youth, improve natural disaster resilience, combat corruption, and counter malign influence from specific authoritarian regimes in designated beneficiary countries across the Caribbean. It authorizes $88,000,000 in appropriations for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2029.

affected_groups.effect: Receive security assistance, equipment, training, infrastructure support, economic and workforce development programs, and natural disaster resilience programs.
affected_groups.group: Beneficiary countries in the Caribbean (Antigua and Barbuda, The Bahamas, Barbados, Dominica, Dominican Republic, Grenad

affected_groups.effect: Required to implement, coordinate, fund, and report on the Caribbean Basin Security Initiative and associated strategies.
affected_groups.group: U.S. Federal Agencies (Department of State, USAID, Department of Justice, Department of Defense)

key_provisions: Authorizes the Caribbean Basin Security Initiative (CBSI) for thirteen specific beneficiary countries in the Caribbean region.
Sets out specific program purposes including maritime and aerial security cooperation, border and port security, law enforcement capacity building, and justice sector reform.
Authorizes $88,000,000 to be appropriated to the Department of State and USAID for each fiscal year from 2025 through 2029.
Requires the Secretary of State and USAID Administrator to submit a detailed implementation plan and annual progress updates to appropriate congressional committees.
Requires programs and strategies to increase natural disaster response and resilience, including sharing best practices and improving rapid-response mechanisms.
Directs efforts to counter malign influence and security assistance from authoritarian regimes such as China, Russia, Iran, Venezuela, Nicaragua, and Cuba.
missing_information: The exact allocation of funds among the thirteen individual beneficiary countries is not specified.
The specific mechanisms or criteria for evaluating high-risk telecommunications vendors are not detailed beyond broad authorization.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 4368 authorizes the Caribbean Basin Security Initiative (CBSI) to be carried out by the Secretary of State and the Administrator of the U.S. Agency for International Development. The bill aims to promote citizen safety, counter transnational criminal organizations, strengthen law enforcement and the rule of law, prevent crime among at-risk youth, improve natural disaster resilience, combat corruption, and counter malign influence from specific authoritarian regimes in designated beneficiary countries across the Caribbean. It authorizes $88,000,000 in appropriations for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2029.
summary_detail.significance: This bill establishes a multi-year statutory authorization and funding level of $88 million annually from fiscal years 2025 through 2029 for security, anti-corruption, and disaster resilience programs across thirteen Caribbean nations, backed by required multi-agency implementation plans and reporting.
